record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: For coupled systems in which one unknown ψ satisfies i∂tψ = -∆ψ + V(x)ψ + F(x,t,u)ψ and u is governed by another equation, how can one identify mathematically interesting coupled models, prove a priori estimates tailored to those models, and define channel wave operators for each unknown such as ψ and u so that the large-time decomposition into a free wave plus a weakly localized part can be established?

evidence.quote: This raises the question of how to identify interesting models of systems of equations and establish a priory estimates tailored to the system. In particular, it may be necessary to devise a suitable definition of channel wave operators for each of the unknown functions ψ,u .

artifact.category_tag: channel wave operators for coupled dispersive systems
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a coupled system of evolution equations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ (for some spatial dimension $d \ge 1$) of the form
\[
\begin{cases}
i\,\partial_t \psi(x,t) = -\Delta \psi(x,t) + V(x)\,\psi(x,t) + F(x,t,u)\,\psi(x,t), \\
\mathcal{L}(u) = G(x,t,\psi,u),
\end{cases}
\]
where $V:\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ is a (suitably decaying) real-valued potential, $F$ is a nonlinear coupling depending on the second unknown $u$, $\mathcal{L}$ is a dispersive or wave-type differential operator governing $u$, and $G$ couples the dynamics of $u$ back to $\psi$.

By a channel wave operator for $\psi$ one means a (possibly nonlinear) map that, given an asymptotic profile $\psi_+$, produces a global solution $\psi(x,t)$ of the coupled system such that, as $t \to +\infty$, $\psi$ admits a large-time decomposition
\[
\psi(x,t) = e^{it\Delta}\psi_+(x) + \psi_{\mathrm{wl}}(x,t) + o_{L^2}(1),
\]
where $\psi_{\mathrm{wl}}$ is a weakly localized remainder (i.e., a remainder whose time-averaged energy concentrates in bounded regions of space). Analogously for $u$ relative to the free flow of $\mathcal{L}$.

Problem. Identify classes of physically or mathematically natural couplings $(F,G,\mathcal{L})$ for which:
(a) global-in-time a priori estimates tailored to the coupled structure can be established for finite-energy solutions $(\psi,u)$;
(b) channel wave operators can be defined for each of the unknowns $\psi$ and $u$; and
(c) every finite-energy solution admits, as $t \to +\infty$, a decomposition into a free (linear) asymptotic wave plus a weakly localized component, simultaneously for $\psi$ and for $u$.

In particular, formulate precise hypotheses on $V$, $F$, $G$, and $\mathcal{L}$ under which such a coupled asymptotic decomposition holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns a recently proposed paradigm of channel wave operators and weakly localized remainders in scattering theory, extended to coupled systems. No published work appears to resolve the general program for coupled models; it is posed as a direction for future research, and current literature only addresses related single-equation or specific coupled cases. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Review listing open problems including the extension of channel wave operator techniques to coupled systems of equations.
status_evidence.claim: The coupled-system scattering decomposition with channel wave operators is listed as an open problem.
